newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks to decide working capital loans in '98.
newsitem.headline: China banks to decide working capital loans in '98.

text.p: China's commercial banks will from next year have the authority to decide the size of working capital loans based on their asset-liability ratio and performance, central bank officials said.

From 1998, the central bank, the People's Bank of China, will no longer set quarterly limits on working capital loans by the four state commercial banks but will indirectly supervise operations, the China Daily Business Weekly on Sunday quoted officials as saying.
The system has already been successfully implemented in 12 smaller commercial banks, the newspaper said.
The central bank sets quarterly credit quotas for the Bank of China, the China Construction Bank, the Agricultural Bank of China and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
From this year the central bank will check the volume of working capital loans at the end of the first half, the third quarter and at the year end, the newspaper said.
That will offer more flexibility for commercial banks and force them to improve controls, it said.
Controls over fixed capital credits will be lifted by 2000.
